h: Tips for a winning seaside session
p: First-timers often swing far too hard. The machine rewards timing more than muscle, so start on an easier setting, watch the ball onto the bat and work your way up. It's also worth taking a couple of looseners before the scoring really starts, especially if your group is competitive. Players who've stood in a net before will be right at home, but the scoring and screens mean beginners can get a real buzz from their very first clean hit.

With a family, think about mixing ages across teams so the grown-ups aren't always beating the kids (or, more likely, the other way round). A little prize for the winners, even an ice cream on the seafront afterwards, keeps everyone keen until the last ball.

Bournemouth gives you heaps of ways to round off a day. The Lower Gardens run down from the town centre to the seafront and are lovely for a stroll, with the Oceanarium aquarium right by the pier at Pier Approach. Boscombe has its own pier and a more laid-back feel, and the Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum, set in a striking Victorian clifftop villa on the East Cliff, is a real gem for a calmer hour. If you've got a car, Hengistbury Head offers big views over Christchurch Harbour, and Poole and Sandbanks are just along the coast.
